examples.question_text:
Complete each equivalent ratio.
a. $4:9=20:\square$
b. $18:42=\square:7$
examples.solution_text:
a. $20\div4=5$, so multiply both parts by $5$.
$4:9=(4\times5):(9\times5)=20:45$
b. $42\div7=6$, so divide both parts by $6$.
$18:42=(18\div6):(42\div6)=3:7$

a. $28\div7=4$. Multiply both parts by $4$.
$5:7=20:28$
b. $28\div7=4$. Divide both parts by $4$.
$16:28=(16\div4):(28\div4)=4:7$

examples.question_text:
a. A student says $5:8$ and $9:12$ are equivalent because $4$ was added to both parts. Explain the mistake and give an equivalent ratio to $5:8$.
b. Show that $18:30$ and $27:45$ are equivalent by writing both as the same ratio.
examples.solution_text:
a. Multiplying $5$ by $1.8$ gives $9$, but multiplying $8$ by $1.8$ gives $14.4$, not $12$. Adding $4$ has changed the comparison.
Multiplying both original parts by $3$ gives $5:8=15:24$.
b. Multiply both parts of $18:30$ by $3$: $18:30=54:90$.
Multiply both parts of $27:45$ by $2$: $27:45=54:90$.
Both give $54:90$, so the ratios are equivalent.

examples.question_text:
Complete each equivalent ratio.
a. $8:12=20:\square$
b. $6:15=x:25$. Find $x$.
examples.solution_text:
a. $20\div8=2.5$. Multiply both parts by $2.5$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}8:12\\&=(8\times2.5):(12\times2.5)\\&=20:30\end{aligned}$
b. $25\div15=\frac{5}{3}$. Multiply both parts by $\frac{5}{3}$.
$\begin{aligned}x&=6\times\frac{5}{3}\\&=10\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text:
a. Complete $30:42=25:\square$.
b. Which of $15:21$, $15:19$ and $12:18$ is equivalent to $10:14$? Show your working.
examples.solution_text:
a. Divide both parts by $6$, then multiply both parts by $5$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}30:42\\&=(30\div6):(42\div6)\\&=5:7\\&=(5\times5):(7\times5)\\&=25:35\end{aligned}$
b. Divide both parts by $2$, then multiply both parts by $3$.
$\begin{aligned}&\mathrel{\phantom{=}}10:14\\&=(10\div2):(14\div2)\\&=5:7\\&=(5\times3):(7\times3)\\&=15:21\end{aligned}$
The equivalent ratio is $15:21$.
